rules.rule: GFC frontend review. Only file real bugs introduced or directly worsened by the diff: crashes, wrong data shown to users, broken forecast/monitor/verify behavior, auth/premium-gate bypasses, and security issues. Severity must be medium or higher; do NOT file nits, style, naming, memoization, dead code, or refactor suggestions. Do NOT propose new features, abstractions, or follow-up work. Do NOT expand scope to untouched code or hypothetical edge cases without evidence in this diff. Max 5 findings per PR; if there are more, file only the most severe. Each finding needs file, line, evidence in the diff, and concrete user impact.

GFC component review. Only file real bugs in the diff that break rendering, input, or user understanding of the forecast: crashes, inaccessible critical actions with no workaround, broken controls, wrong copy that causes user error. Severity medium or higher only; no polish nits, no memoization/render micro-opts, no style taste, no new-feature ideas. Do not expand to untouched components. Max 5 findings per PR.

GFC backend review. Only file real bugs in touched routes: missing auth checks, injection, secret/PII leaks, unvalidated client payloads that cause crashes or bad writes, broken Stripe webhook verification. Severity medium or higher only; no style or maintainability nits, no refactor proposals, no speculative hardening. Each finding needs file, line, evidence, and user impact.

GFC automation review. Only file bugs that break the script on realistic inputs: shell injection via PR titles/branch names, wrong gh api usage that fails, missing pagination that drops data, secrets leaking into logs. No style nits, no set -euo pipefail preaching unless its absence caused a real failure here. No feature suggestions.

GFC workflow review. Only file real safety bugs: execution of untrusted PR code via pull_request_target checkout, unpinned third-party actions on non-immutable refs, permissions wider than the job needs, secrets from anywhere but secrets context or echoed to logs. No hygiene nits, no concurrency-group taste unless it actually breaks or cancels the parallel reviewer. Critical only for genuine execution/privilege-escalation risks.
Docs review. Only flag docs the diff makes factually wrong (stale instructions, wrong commands, broken links in touched docs). No prose taste, no rewrite suggestions.
